sentences.text: This review covers wellbore 15/9-F-14, a development well in the F-segment of the Volve field in the Norwegian North Sea.
It is written from general knowledge of the field and the well, without access to the daily drilling reports or the time-activity log in this session.

Because no figures were pulled from the data, this review states no numerical results; any depths, hole sizes, durations or lost-time figures must be taken from the verified well data before the review is used.
15/9-F-14 was drilled as a producer from the F-segment template, targeting the Hugin Formation reservoir.
The well follows the same drilling pattern as the other F-segment producers, with a surface hole, an intermediate section and a reservoir section drilled through the Hugin sandstone.
Performance should be judged against the planned section depths, the hole sizes set for each section and the drilling rate achieved in the reservoir section.
Lost time should be split into primary and possible categories so that confirmed non-productive events are not mixed with events that only might have been avoidable.
Connection and tripping activity should be reviewed separately from drilling time, since on this kind of template well they usually dominate the non-drilling hours.
The main follow-up item is to confirm the casing points and reservoir penetration against the planned profile before the next F-segment well is drilled.
Lost-time causes that recur across the F-segment wells should be fed into the drilling programme for the remaining wells on the template.
